topic: Dhaka 4th worst in global air quality
headline_marked: [[Dhaka ranks 4th in global air quality index]], indicating unhealthy air
headline: Dhaka ranks 4th in global air quality index, indicating unhealthy air
summary: Dhaka's air quality has been consistently poor, posing significant health risks to its residents. The city frequently appears among the worst globally for air pollution.
details: Dhaka has been listed as the fourth worst city globally in the Air Quality Index (AQI), with its air quality rated as "unhealthy." This ranking highlights the persistent challenge of air pollution faced by the capital.

The AQI, a measure of daily air quality, indicates the level of air pollution and its associated health risks. A higher AQI value signifies a greater level of air pollution and a higher risk to public health.

Exposure to such poor air quality can lead to various health issues, including respiratory problems, heart disease, and other chronic conditions. Vulnerable populations, such as children and the elderly, are particularly at risk.
Major contributors to Dhaka's air pollution include vehicle emissions, dust from construction sites, industrial pollution, and smoke from brick kilns, especially during the dry season.

topic: Missing madrasa students in Sylhet, ransom demand
headline_marked: [[Ransom demanded for two missing Sylhet madrasa students]] after video call shows beating
headline: Ransom demanded for two missing Sylhet madrasa students after video call shows beating
summary: Two 15-year-old madrasa students have been missing for three days in Sylhet. Their parents received a video call showing one of them being beaten, along with a demand for BDT 1 lakh ransom.
details: Two madrasa students in Sylhet have been missing for three days. The father of one student received a video call showing his son being beaten, accompanied by a demand for BDT 1 lakh.

The missing students are Tamim Ahmed and Sayeed Masud Chowdhury (Nayeem), both 15 years old. They were studying in the Hifz section of Jabale Noor Hafizia Madrasa and Orphanage in Khadim Para, Sylhet.
Guardians, madrasa authorities, and police confirmed that the two left the madrasa during Fajr prayers on Tuesday morning. They remained untraceable until Thursday night.
Sayeed's father, Bebul Ahmed, received a voice message and a video via Imo from an unknown account. The video allegedly showed Nayeem tied up and being assaulted.
The perpetrators demanded BDT 1 lakh through a bKash number, threatening to kill Sayeed if the ransom was not paid. Bebul Ahmed promptly reported the incident to the police.

Tamim's father, Abdus Sattar, stated that his son had previously left the madrasa twice without informing them. He expressed deep concern for his son's well-being, saying "Allah knows if my son is alive."

Shahparan Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Ferdous Ahmed confirmed that both guardians and madrasa authorities have filed a General Diary (GD). Police have circulated photographs of the two students nationwide as part of their efforts.

Regarding the Imo ransom demand, the OC noted that the associated phone number has been inactive for a year. He added that fraudsters often exploit missing persons cases, and the video sent was unclear, but investigations are ongoing.
